cases.input: My car won't start on the M25 hard shoulder and I have AA breakdown cover. What should I do?
cases.actual_output:
Sorry to hear that! Don't worry, we're here to help. Since you're on the M25 hard shoulder, please make sure you're in a safe location, away from traffic, and turn on your hazard lights.

To get assistance, please follow these steps:

1. Check your AA policy to see if you have breakdown cover that includes roadside assistance. If you're unsure, you can check your policy documents or the AA app.
2. If you have breakdown cover, please call our emergency number: 0800 88 77 66 (don't worry about the cost, as it's included in your policy).
3. Our team will ask for some basic information, such as your name, membership number, and location. Please have these details ready.
4. We'll then send a breakdown expert to your location to help you get back on the road. If you need a tow or other assistance, we'll arrange that too.

Remember to stay safe and avoid any potential hazards while waiting for our team to arrive. If you're in immediate danger or need urgent assistance, please call 999 or the emergency services.

We'll do our best to get you back on the move as quickly as possible.
cases.expected_output: First get to safety: pull as far to the left as you can with your wheels turned to the left, switch on your hazard lights, and get everyone out through the left-hand doors. Stand behind the barrier on the verge, away from traffic, and put on a high-vis jacket if you have one. Don't attempt any repair on a motorway. Then report the breakdown by calling the AA on 03330 046 046 (on a motorway use the phone, not the app). Look for a driver location sign or marker post to give your position. An AA patrol will come to try to fix the car at the roadside, and if it can't be fixed there you may be recovered depending on your cover.

cases.input: I've got a flat tyre and no spare. Will an AA patrol fix it and will I have to pay for a new tyre?
cases.actual_output:
Sorry to hear that you've got a flat tyre! As an AA breakdown assistance virtual assistant, I'm here to help.

If you're a member of the AA, our patrols are trained to help with a wide range of breakdowns, including flat tyres. If you're unable to continue driving safely, our patrol will do their best to help you get back on the road.

Regarding the flat tyre, our patrol will assess the situation and provide guidance on the best course of action. If the tyre is repairable, they may be able to repair it on the spot. However, if the tyre is damaged beyond repair or you don't have a spare, they may recommend calling a local garage or tyre fitter to replace the tyre.

As for the cost of a new tyre, it will depend on the type of tyre and the garage or tyre fitter you choose. Our patrol will not be able to provide a new tyre, but they can help you find a local garage or tyre fitter to do the job. You will need to pay for the new tyre and any labour costs separately.

Remember to always check your policy or the AA app for specific details on what's covered and what's not. If you're unsure about your breakdown cover or what's included, feel free to ask!
cases.expected_output: An AA patrol will come out and try to get you mobile, for example with a tyre sealant or by recovering the car to a nearby garage if it can't be made safe at the roadside. Patrols don't carry replacement tyres, so the cost of a new tyre or garage repair isn't part of standard cover. If you have added Tyre Cover, the AA can help towards eligible repair or replacement costs up to £160 per tyre, subject to that cover's terms.
